sourceOccurrences.note: The product law, open graph, connection, cluster, two-point and extended susceptibility definitions are linked to the existing product-model, connectivity and susceptibility articles. Q0D1 and 0N0J explain adjacency, monotonicity, reflexive/symmetric/transitive connections, singleton clusters and non-vacuity on two vertices. GUHT and the concluding paragraph separate fixed-list cylinders and deterministic witness/escape identities from countable measurability. The source defines total measure expressions for arbitrary vertex types; the article uses probability terminology for connection and cluster observables only under its stated measurability hypotheses. Abbreviations and the probability-measure instance are not in the explicit definition/theorem count.

proofUses.reason: Taking the reciprocal of the positive component size in the root-sum identity counts each component once.
Opening a pair merges only its endpoint components; monotone coupling compares profiles, with diagonal erasure for the off-diagonal extension.
Group ordered root tuples by their distinct full-cluster intersections, apply the multi-cluster product bound, and expand the generating function in falling factorials.
Extend the finite-valued discovery comparison to observed block sizes, pass joint-tail inequalities through eventual agreement of the finite-window partition, and compare exponential moments.
Bound the centered exponential remainder separately for negative and positive parameters, then optimize the exponential Markov inequality.
Grouping the root sum by the window partition gives the identity and elementary bounds; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
The distinct-cluster comparison conditions on an explored cluster and couples the outside product law; the covariance lower bound applies Harris (X5SS) to the increasing observables T_F and T_G.
